data.long_meaning: Derived from the Latin word 'nelum' meaning 'nutmeg tree'. Nelia is a name of Latin origin, commonly used in the Christian tradition as a given name for girls. The name may also be considered to symbolize the spiritual journey towards enlightenment, as the sun is often seen as a symbol of the divine.

in_hebrew.name: נליה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: נליה היא שם נשי שמקורו ביוונית עתיקה, ומשמעותו 'אלוהים' או 'קדוש'. השם נמצא בברית החדשה בשם של אחת מהאם-טיפוס של הבישוף-אפוסטול מרקוס, 'נליה' (Νελλια). השם נודע גם בכינוי 'נליה-הבכורה', 'נליה-הצדיקה', 'נליה-הטובה' ו'נליה-הזכורה'.

in_greek.name: Νελλία
in_greek.long_meaning: Η Νελλία είναι γυναικείο όνομα αρχαίας ελληνικής καταγωγής, που σημαίνει 'θεοί' ή 'αγία'. Το όνομα αναφέρεται στη Βίβλο της Καινής Διαθήκης ως το όνομα μιας από τις μητέρες του μαθητή της Μαρίας, 'Νελλία' (Νελλία). Το όνομα έχει επίσης άλλες μορφές, όπως 'Νελλία-η προκοπής', 'Νελλία-η σοφία', 'Νελλία-η ευσεβία' και 'Νελλία-η θεία'.

in_latin.name: Nelia
in_latin.long_meaning: Nelia est nomen femininum originis Graecae antiquae, significans 'dei' vel 'sacrum'. Nomen in Novo Testamento citatur in nomine una e matribus discipuli Mariae, 'Nelia' (Nellia). Nomen habet etiam alias formas, ut 'Nelia-primogenita', 'Nelia-sapientia', 'Nelia-pietas' et 'Nelia-divina'.

historical_references.reference: There is a 6th-century Byzantine saint named Pelagia of Antioch, who was originally named Pelagia but later changed her name to Nea (which means 'new' in Greek) after she was miraculously cured of leprosy. Her new name was later Latinized to Nelia.

In medieval Spain, there was a town named Nelida (now known as Nuévalos) which was believed to have been named after Santo Nelio, a local Christian saint. Santo Nelio is believed to have lived in the 3rd century and was a military officer who, along with his companions, was martyred during the persecution of Christians under the Roman Emperor Maximian.
